text: A spanning set of a vector space V that is also linearly independent is called a ___; for a finite-dimensional V, every such set has the same number of elements, namely dim(V).
explanation: A basis is a linearly independent spanning set (equivalently, a minimal spanning set or a maximal independent set). A spanning set on its own may be redundant and larger than a basis, while an independent set on its own may fail to span. The invariance of the cardinality of a basis is exactly what makes the dimension well defined.
